== Biography ==
Anges was born in 1725 and died in 1801.


Agnes married John Snoddy on 7 Oct 1741 in First Presbyterian Church, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (John Snoddy was born about 1720 in County Antrim, Ireland, died in Feb 1784 in Abbington, Washington County, Virginia and was buried in Walton Mountain, Blount County, Tennessee.<ref>https://web.archive.org/web/2006*/http://www.davidleas.com/leas%20family%20genealogy/9549.htm</ref>

* Born: 7 Dec 1725, Irvine, Ayr, Scotland
* Marriage (1): John Snoddy on 7 Oct 1741 in First Presbyterian Church, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
* Died: 30 Dec 1801, Witt's Foundry, Jefferson County, Tennessee at age 76
* Buried: Leadville, Tennessee
    
Agnes Glasgow's father was William Glasgow and her mother was Margaret Montfodd/Montfort. From Elaine Comes: "William GLasgow had a brother named Hugh who married Janet Kilpatrick. They were sons of John Glasgow and Agnes Spark."



It has been told that Agnes met John Snoddy on their journey to American. Agnes and John supposedly fell in love on board the ship and married not long after arriving in America. Agnes Glasgow's birth taken from Scotland Files, Irvine, Ayr, Scotland, Church of L.D.S. Batch C115952, Input 2326, printout 1041383. This image file appears to be from a vestry book recording births.


The first eight children were born in Pennsylvania and the last three were born in Virginia.

7. Cary Snoddy.....Born August 6, 1755. Died June 12, 1822.

9. Alice Snoddy.....Born 1759. Died 1789.

William Glasgow Snoddy was born on June 22, 1763 in Buckingham County, Virginia. He married Sarah Davis on December 22, 1785. Sarah was the daughter of John Davis and Mary Allison. She was born in 1767 in Washington County, Virginia. William died on March 3, 1834 in Virginia.

They had eleven children:

October 7, 1859.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1055]] is assessed at 99% (proved). Agnes’s 1725 transcript explicitly names Wm and Margaret Montford; the same Irvine couple recurs in 1724 and 1729. Her later Snoddy identity is a different proposition.

Existing child-to-father link assessed from held public evidence; The account expressly represents the Irvine adult; his Stevenston childhood and Dundonald-weaver identity are separate hypotheses.

Next useful test: Inspect OPR595/1 p37; test later Agnes identity independently.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574073&tab=this Agnes Glasgow, 07 Dec 1725, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
